issues.detail: The Vietnamese phrase 'là kẻ đã được định trước' (who/which was predestined) incorrectly identifies the subject of the predestination. In the Greek, 'προορισθεντες' (predestined) is a nominative plural participle modifying 'εμείς' (we), meaning 'we were predestined.' The Vietnamese construction makes it sound as if the 'inheritance' or a third person was predestined.

The Greek 'εν ω' (in whom) is rendered as 'Trong Ngài', but the phrase 'εκληρωθημεν' (we have inherited/received an inheritance) is slightly compressed. More importantly, the Vietnamese fails to clearly link 'predestined' back to 'us' as the subject.
